purpose: Render and validate independent ownership-bound, expiring AWS demo cleanup before runtime provisioning

initialRepairedFailures: Typed runtime-environment literals, group IDs, test path resolution and replacement callback annotation.
Four repeated-array lookup diagnostics and two async-loop diagnostics were repaired using sets and fixed-size batches with bounded SDK sockets, without suppression.
Final input review added eight cases rejecting trailing line terminators in manifest identities and a hosted-zone regression.
Three final service cases distinguish a zero-task INACTIVE record with removed tags from active or nonzero-task unowned records.

limitations: No stack, role, schedule, secret parameter, certificate, runtime, flags or production migrations were created or enabled.
Actual prepared-manifest change-set validation, deployed guard inspection/armed invocation and real teardown proof remain required.
The future workload template must fit the cleanup IAM boundary, use implicit caller credentials, and prohibit standalone tasks/autoscaling.
EC2 group replacement has no compare-and-swap; the worker/ENI ownership lease must exclude concurrent network writers.
IAM simulation and local inline Lambda execution do not establish deployed IAM, CloudFormation deletion or AWS network behavior.
Teardown is not a hard AWS billing cap; full workload, traffic/storage, cost-admission and hosted acceptance gates remain.
